title: MaleCNS-derived graded T4 direction-selectivity circuit
question: Can a MaleCNS-derived T4 motion circuit distinguish the direction of a moving visual stimulus in the biologically expected way?
result_sentence: For the selected adjacent-column edge, the graded MaleCNS circuit produces stronger forward than reverse T4a activity and stronger reverse than forward T4b activity; removing the direct inhibitory T4-input pathway reduces the order contrast by 82.3%.
scope_qualification: This supports direction selectivity within the stated reduced model; it is not yet an experimental validation of fly T4 voltage or behavior.
validation_scope: Frozen-parameter spatial validation only; no dynamics, connectivity-selection, sign, stimulus, or node-set changes were made.
changed_from_exp001: Replaced spike-gated propagation with continuous graded state propagation.
Represented an ON-edge L1 release deviation with receptor-mediated sign inversion into Mi1/Tm3.
Added the MaleCNS direct T4 input classes Mi4, Mi9, C3, and CT1 alongside Mi1/Tm3.
Integrated excitatory Mi1/Tm3 and inhibitory Mi4/Mi9/C3/CT1 signals continuously at T4.
Added a direct inhibitory-input ablation control.
why_changed: EXP-001 executed correctly but its spike-gated abstraction stopped at subthreshold Mi1/Tm3 activity, so T4 direction selectivity could not be evaluated.

anatomy.edge_weight: MaleCNS synapse_count, normalized by total modeled input mass per postsynaptic node

answer_leakage_audit.normalization_rule: Each postsynaptic node divides fixed signed MaleCNS synapse-count mass by its total modeled input mass; the denominator is identical across temporal-order conditions.

class_specific_rules.rule: L1 -> Mi1/Tm3 is receptor-inverted from negative ON-edge release deviation to positive postsynaptic drive.
Mi1/Tm3 are positive T4 inputs; Mi4/C3/CT1 are negative T4 inputs; Mi9 is treated as a negative receptor pathway and is not directly driven by the ON-only event.
Tm3 and Mi1 use different fixed time constants, with Mi1 slower/delayed than Tm3; inhibitory drive uses one fixed delay and time constant.
Fast excitation and delayed inhibition are represented as separate spatially weighted channels.

answer_leakage_audit.conclusion: No explicit T4a/T4b/T4c/T4d answer key, condition branch, pair-specific tuning, or fitted output transform was found. The observed preference is emergent within the retained MaleCNS connectivity and these independently motivated class rules. It is not a full-connectome result because the inhibitory visual drive is an exogenous delayed channel and not every upstream branch is materialized.
answer_leakage_audit.numeric_parameter_caveat: The cited literature motivates qualitative sign and timing relationships; the exact frozen time constants and 15 ms delay are explicit phenomenological assumptions, not measured biophysical constants and not fit to validation results.

geometry_validation.workbook_mapping: positive step in the second ROW_COL grid index on the right-eye optic-column assignment workbook
geometry_validation.reason_unresolved: The official MaleCNS supplemental workbook publishes column identifiers, L1 IDs, and column annotations, but not a mapping from the two suffix indices to front/back, dorsal/ventral, or the T4a-d cardinal labels. Therefore the experiment is reported in workbook-grid coordinates only.
geometry_validation.known_t4_reference: Primary literature describes T4a-d as four cardinal direction channels near the central eye, but that does not by itself map this MaleCNS workbook axis to a body-axis label.
geometry_validation.grid_axis_result: The second-index direction favors T4a over T4b; the first-index direction favors T4c over T4d in the held-out means, with one small T4d exception.

physiology_basis.use: Mi1 and Tm3 are graded ON-pathway responses with different temporal dynamics; Mi1 is delayed relative to Tm3.
L1 glutamatergic input is sign-inverted in Mi1/Tm3 through receptor-mediated physiology rather than a simple body-level transmitter sign.
Mi1/Tm3 provide major excitatory T4 input; Mi4/C3/CT1 provide inhibitory input; Mi9 is glutamatergic and receptor-sign dependent; input locations are spatially segregated across T4 dendrites.
T4 direction selectivity combines fast excitation with spatially offset, delayed inhibition.
Connectome-constrained mechanistic models can use measured connectivity plus explicit dynamics, while unknown physiology must remain a model assumption rather than being hidden in weights.

model_assumptions: L1 ON-edge release is represented as a negative graded release deviation, followed by a negative receptor transform into a positive Mi1/Tm3 response.
Mi1/Tm3 are excitatory at T4; Mi4/C3/CT1 are inhibitory at T4; Mi9 is treated as an inhibitory receptor pathway but is not directly driven by the ON-only stimulus.
The retained MaleCNS L1->Mi1/Tm3 and input->T4 paths provide a two-column coordinate; missing coordinates use a midpoint fallback.
Direct inhibitory T4 inputs are driven by a delayed, low-pass visual channel because the first local model does not yet materialize every upstream photoreceptor/L1/L3 branch.
The output is a dimensionless graded activity proxy, not calibrated membrane voltage in mV and not a spike count.

held_out_spatial_validation.interpretation: The original T4a/T4b pattern generalizes across the sampled second-index pairs, while the orthogonal first-index pairs show the complementary T4c/T4d pattern. This is spatially structured but cannot be named front/back or dorsal/ventral from the MaleCNS workbook alone.

matched_control.control: same-count T4 -> downstream structural null; these edges have no sign in the frozen feed-forward T4 readout
matched_control.qualification: This is a matched negative control for the current feed-forward readout, not a claim that downstream T4 connectivity is biologically irrelevant in a larger model.

controls: Reverse the identical two-column stimulus order.
Remove all modeled Mi4/Mi9/C3/CT1 -> T4 inhibitory edges while leaving the MaleCNS excitatory graph unchanged.
Repeat across three additional adjacent row-2 column pairs.
Repeat across four held-out first-index pairs and four held-out second-index pairs.
Remove a matched count of T4-to-downstream structural edges; peak order contrast is unchanged.
limitations: Absolute visual-axis mapping of workbook coordinates to canonical T4a/b/c/d directions is not yet independently calibrated.
T4 dendritic synapse locations are not present in the MaleCNS export used here; spatial offsets are represented through retained path coordinates and explicit model assumptions.
The model does not yet include a photoreceptor/luminance transduction model or all upstream L1/L3 branches.
Mi9 receptor sign and ON/OFF recruitment remain unresolved in this experiment.
The result is not a FlyGym, behavior, training, or optimization result.
generated_outputs_policy: Bulk traces, downloaded MaleCNS data, caches, and environments remain ignored by Git; this compact record is the public result summary.
